verdict.rationale: GitLab documents group-level AI governance for monitoring agent sessions and audit logs, and per-run session execution data. It also states that agent activities are attributed in audit logs and commit histories. However, the documented attribution is to a service account, and no evidence explicitly ties logged agent actions back to the human user who triggered them. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that audit entries record the triggering user alongside the agent identity, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the audit trail.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can audit AI agent sessions and actions attributed to the user who triggered them

citations.quote: Monitor AI agent sessions, audit logs, and developer exposure across a group.
All agent activities are clearly attributed to a service account, making it easy to identify automated actions in audit logs and commit histories.
Sessions show the status and execution data for the agents and flows you’ve run.
Record Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex sessions with the GitLab CLI so they appear on the dashboard as ECAs.
